subject: Close velocity anchor, procurement safeguard & MAP milestones
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Timeline impact — procurement vendor shortlist delay

Marcus,

Quick heads-up from procurement: the vendor shortlist review just got pushed by two weeks (internal compliance flagged an extra due diligence step). That pushes our evaluation window out — the earliest the team can do PoC interviews is the week of 5/31 now. I know that moves our previously-discussed close target.

Can Redwood do a short MAP update with staged acceptance options? Procurement is sensitive to commitment language — they want clear acceptance gates tied to specific deliverables. I attached the RFP (ACME_RFP_v2.pdf) and have procurement on cc for details.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Strategic Sourcing
Acme Corporation
(attachment: ACME_RFP_v2.pdf (pdf))

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline impact — procurement vendor shortlist delay

Samira,

Appreciate the heads-up. We can absolutely update the MAP to reflect a staged acceptance plan and specific procurement gating language. Two immediate asks so we can move fast:

- procurement's preferred list of PoC stakeholders (names/emails) so we can schedule sessions the week of 5/31
- which acceptance gates are deal-critical vs. nice-to-have (e.g., SLA latency target at 95th pct vs. extended QA windows)

I'll draft a short risk log entry documenting the slip and propose an "anchor date" for commercial close with a rollback trigger if procurement can't get the shortlist finalized by 6/08. Draft MAP_v3 (spreadsheet) will be attached once we align.

Proposed next steps: short sync (15m) tomorrow with procurement + product + solutions engineering to lock milestones. Is 10:30am PT good?

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: none yet)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline impact — procurement vendor shortlist delay

Folks,

Recommend we do two things in parallel:

1) Anchor: set a commercial anchor date (e.g., 2027-06-15) that we communicate as the target close, but explicitly attach a "rollback trigger" — procurement not finalizing shortlist or no PoC participants confirmed by 2027-06-08 will move us to contingency lane.

2) Thermostat risk scoring on the MAP: low/medium/high entries for schedule, procurement, legal, and integration. Each risk gets an owner and a remediation step with SLAs (48h for procurement follow-up, 72h for legal clarifications).

I'll attach a short risk log template and sample scoring — use it to populate the MAP so execs can quickly judge severity.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachment: risk_log_template.xlsx (spreadsheet))

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline impact — procurement vendor shortlist delay

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks. Procurement confirmed they need the additional vendor diligence step; that pushes internal calendar but not the overall desire to close this quarter. Important constraints:

- PoC panel availability: earliest 5/31–6/02 window (mornings preferred)
- Contracting: procurement requires a conditional acceptance clause for split acceptance (staged delivery) and an audit log retention explanation before legal will sign off
- If we cannot demonstrate PoC sessions by 6/08, procurement will move to a two-week internal re-vet and may require an executive sponsor call (i.e., escalation to VP Sourcing)

We are open to a staged acceptance approach, but need the MAP to show measurable gates and a fallback credit or short-term pilot pricing if the final acceptance is delayed.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Strategic Sourcing, Acme Corporation

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>, Jordan Mills <jmills@capitalsolutions.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: MAP_v3 + contingency options for procurement constraint

Team / Samira,

Attached are two docs: MAP_v3.xlsx (milestones + risk scoring) and contingency_offers.docx (three low-effort scope reductions with proposed credit windows).

Summary of the contingency lane (short):
- Staged acceptance: Accept core inference API + telemetry in month 1, defer full integrations (SAML, custom routing) to month 2.
- Pilot pricing credit: If final acceptance slips beyond 2027-06-15, Redwood offers a 20% credit on month-1 invoice for each full week past the anchor date until acceptance (capped at 6 weeks).
- Procurement safeguard: a clause allowing Acme to pause rollout and receive a rollback to the pilot config if integration regressions appear during staged acceptance (documented bug SLA).

I populated the risk log with an initial "schedule" risk = HIGH (probability 0.6, impact medium-high) and assigned owners. Please review and flag changes.

(attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), contingency_offers.docx (docx))

- Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Updated MAP + anchor proposition (request: sign-off on gates)

Samira / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clarity. I've uploaded MAP_v3 to the DocuSign link below with the following key items summarized:

- Anchor date: 2027-06-15 (commercial close target)
- Rollback trigger: absence of confirmed PoC stakeholders & scheduled sessions by 2027-06-08 moves the deal to contingency lane (pilot pricing + staged acceptance)
- Acceptance gates: PoC completion, SLA validation, security checklist (audit log retention + KMS plan)
- Contingency offer: pilot credit schedule as proposed by Priyom (20% per week cap up to 6 weeks)

Action items:
1) Procurement to confirm PoC participants and availability by 2027-05-28
2) Acme legal to confirm audit-log/KMS clarifications by 2027-06-01
3) Redwood to prepare an exec summary for an escalation call if rollback trigger fires

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/agree/map-v3
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/0/record/ACME-2027-017

Please countersign the MAP or reply with suggested edits by EOD 2027-05-28 so we can lock calendars.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated MAP + anchor proposition (request: sign-off on gates)

Marcus —

Thanks for the fast turn. We reviewed MAP_v3 and the contingency offers. Procurement is comfortable with the anchor/rollback framework — we will confirm PoC stakeholders by Friday 5/28. Legal asked one clarification on the audit log retention period (they prefer 2 years; can Redwood confirm configurable retention policy and KMS controls in writing?).

Also a commercial note: procurement asked if the pilot credit can be applied as a one-time invoice credit instead of weekly reductions (they prefer cleaner billing). Can you ask finance if that's an option? If yes, we can avoid the exec-escalation path.

Samira Khan
Head of Strategic Sourcing, Acme Corporation
(attachment: none)
